catalogue: Australian internal door leaves, frames, trim and hardware

objects.name: internal door construction system
objects.definition: The coordinated internal door leaves, frames, trim, hinges, sliding or folding gear, latches, locks, pulls, stops, closers and junctions used to close or control an opening between indoor spaces.
functions: Open and close an internal passage or cupboard opening
Coordinate the leaf, frame, movement hardware and operating hardware
Keep physical construction separate from accessibility, fire, acoustic and sanitary performance evidence

ncc_references.relationship: A fully enclosed sanitary compartment needs the applicable outward-opening, sliding, readily removable or clearance arrangement; that requirement is an assembly configuration, not a new material.

cad.pattern: One coordinated doorset per internal opening, with explicit leaf, frame, movement hardware, operating hardware and trim subassemblies
cad.placement: Within an opening through an internal wall or fixed joinery face
cad.end: Finished leaf, frame, hardware and room-side trim
cad.opening: Preserve the operable opening, swing or slide envelope and required clearances
cad.load: Leaf self-weight and operating loads pass through hinges, pivots or rollers into the frame and supporting wall

notes: The discipline adds construction anatomy around existing livable-housing doorway objects and does not treat every internal doorway as a livable-housing doorway.
NCC edition, jurisdiction, approval date and selected compliance pathway remain project data.

objects.name: internal door leaf construction assembly
objects.definition: The complete internal door leaf build-up, including its face skins or joinery members, core or infill, perimeter frame or lippings, lock reinforcement, openings and finish.
functions: Form the moving barrier across the doorway
Carry hinges, rollers and operating hardware
Expose the selected core, edge and face construction for drawing and scheduling

cad.pattern: Rectangular leaf volume subdivided into faces, core, perimeter and local hardware preparations
cad.placement: Hinged, pivoted, suspended or folded within an internal doorway
cad.opening: Glazing, louvre and hardware cut-outs remain explicit
cad.load: Leaf self-weight transfers through its movement hardware to the supporting frame

notes: Solid, hollow and blockboard cores are alternative constructions, not textures applied to the same hidden geometry.

objects.name: flush internal door leaf
objects.definition: An internal door leaf with substantially flat continuous faces fixed over a framed, cellular, blockboard or solid core rather than exposed stile-and-rail panels.
functions: Provide a flat operable door face
Accept paint, laminate, veneer or another selected finish
Contain the selected core and hardware reinforcement

cad.pattern: One flat-faced rectangular leaf per opening or panel position
cad.placement: Within a swing, sliding or folding internal door assembly
cad.opening: Optional glazing or louvre cut-outs are separate
cad.load: Carries its self-weight through selected hinges, pivots or rollers

notes: Flush describes the faces, not the core, mass, sound rating or fire performance.

objects.name: hollow-core flush internal door leaf
objects.definition: A lightweight flush internal door leaf whose thin face skins are stabilised by a perimeter frame and sparse internal framing or cellular infill rather than a continuous solid core.
functions: Provide a lightweight closure for ordinary internal openings
Carry face skins over a cellular or framed interior
Concentrate hardware fixing into reinforced edge or lock zones

cad.pattern: Thin face layers enclosing perimeter members, local blocks and a lightweight cell field
cad.placement: Ordinary internal swing, sliding or folding door positions allowed by the selected product
cad.opening: Cut-outs require documented reinforcement and are not assumed
cad.load: Self-weight passes through reinforced edge zones rather than the cellular field

notes: Hollow core does not mean the whole interior is empty or suitable for arbitrary hardware fixing.

objects.name: solid-core flush internal door leaf
objects.definition: A flush internal door leaf with a substantially continuous dense core behind its face skins, selected where greater mass, robustness or hardware support is wanted.
functions: Provide a heavier and more robust internal closure
Support hardware through a dense core or documented reinforcement
Contribute mass to a selected acoustic or fire system only when separately evidenced

cad.pattern: Continuous core volume enclosed by face skins and edge lippings
cad.placement: Internal doorway where the selected leaf mass and hardware are supported
cad.opening: Any cut-out follows selected leaf evidence
cad.load: Higher self-weight requires compatible hinges, rollers, frame and wall support

notes: This is the ordinary construction family. The fire-safety catalogue owns the solid-core leaf used in a specific protected-opening path.

objects.name: blockboard-core flush internal door leaf
objects.definition: A flush internal door leaf whose core is built from closely arranged timber strips or blocks faced with sheet material to form a stiff, relatively dense panel.
functions: Provide a stiff flush leaf
Give continuous timber-rich support behind the faces
Carry compatible hinges, locks and pulls

cad.pattern: Parallel timber core strips enclosed by crossbands, faces and perimeter lippings
cad.placement: Swing or sliding internal doorway compatible with leaf mass
cad.opening: Cut-outs follow selected-product preparation
cad.load: Self-weight transfers through movement hardware fixed into documented zones

notes: Blockboard describes a core construction and is not interchangeable with every solid-core product.

objects.name: panelled internal door leaf
objects.definition: An internal door leaf formed as a visible stile-and-rail framework containing one or more solid, sheet, moulded or glazed panels rather than continuous flush faces.
functions: Form an operable joinery-style door
Divide the leaf into structural edge members and infill panels
Provide explicit rails, stiles, muntins and panel geometry

cad.pattern: Perimeter and intermediate joinery members enclosing a set of panel openings
cad.placement: Hinged, sliding or folding internal doorway permitted by the selected leaf
cad.opening: Panels and glazing occupy explicit framed openings
cad.load: Leaf frame carries panel weight and transfers the assembly load to movement hardware

notes: A moulded flush-door skin may imitate panel shapes without having separate structural stiles, rails and panels.

objects.name: internal door leaf stile
objects.definition: A vertical edge or intermediate member in a panelled internal door leaf, including the hinge stile and lock or meeting stile roles.
functions: Form the vertical sides of the leaf frame
Receive hinges, locks or meeting hardware where designed
Frame panels and glazing openings
attributes: hinge, lock, meeting or intermediate role

cad.pattern: Vertical members at leaf edges and selected panel divisions
cad.placement: Within the panelled leaf perimeter
cad.opening: Bounds adjacent panel or glazing openings
cad.load: Transfers rail and panel loads to hinges, pivots or rollers

notes: A leaf stile moves with the door; a jamb stays fixed to the wall opening.

objects.name: internal door leaf top rail
objects.definition: The upper horizontal member joining the stiles of a panelled internal door leaf and closing the top of its panel layout.
functions: Tie the leaf stiles together
Frame the upper panel edge
Receive compatible top pivots or hangers where designed

cad.pattern: One upper horizontal member per stile-and-rail leaf
cad.placement: Across the top of the panelled leaf
cad.opening: Bounds the panel field below
cad.load: Ties stiles and may locally receive selected movement hardware

notes: Top rail is a moving leaf member, not the fixed frame head.

objects.name: internal door leaf intermediate rail
objects.definition: A horizontal member between the top and bottom rails of a panelled internal door leaf, used to divide and support the panel arrangement.
functions: Divide panel or glazing openings
Brace the leaf frame
Provide a local zone for mouldings or operating hardware where designed

cad.pattern: Zero or more horizontal divisions between leaf stiles
cad.placement: At designed panel breaks within the leaf
cad.opening: Bounds panels above and below
cad.load: Transfers panel and local hardware loads into stiles

notes: A lock rail is an intermediate rail with a particular hardware role; the terms are not universal synonyms.

objects.name: internal door leaf bottom rail
objects.definition: The lowest horizontal member joining the stiles of a panelled internal door leaf and closing the bottom of its panel layout.
functions: Tie the stiles at the leaf base
Frame the lower panel edge
Provide local material for compatible bottom pivots or trimming limits

cad.pattern: One lower horizontal member per panelled leaf
cad.placement: Across the bottom of the leaf
cad.opening: Bounds the panel field above
cad.load: Ties stiles and may receive selected bottom-pivot preparation

notes: The bottom rail moves with the leaf; the doorway threshold or floor transition does not.

objects.name: internal door leaf infill panel
objects.definition: A solid, sheet or moulded infill fitted within the stiles, rails or muntins of a panelled internal door leaf.
functions: Close a framed area within the leaf
Provide the selected decorative relief or flat field
Move with the surrounding leaf frame

cad.pattern: One panel in each selected stile-and-rail opening
cad.placement: Captured within grooves or mouldings in the leaf frame
cad.opening: Occupies a panel opening and is not the opening itself
cad.load: Supported by the surrounding leaf frame

notes: Panel can mean either this infill or, colloquially, a whole sliding leaf; context must be stored.

objects.name: internal door leaf muntin
objects.definition: A narrow intermediate member that subdivides panel or glazing openings within a panelled internal door leaf.
functions: Subdivide a larger panel field
Support adjacent panel or glazing edges
Create the selected joinery pattern

cad.pattern: Intermediate grid members between rails and stiles
cad.placement: Within panel or glazing fields
cad.opening: Separates neighbouring infill openings
cad.load: Supports adjacent infill edges and transfers load into the leaf frame

notes: Muntin and mullion usage varies; the review queue preserves the distinction rather than forcing equivalence.

objects.name: door leaf honeycomb core infill
objects.definition: A lightweight cellular web placed between the face skins of a hollow-core door leaf to separate and stabilise them over the field of the leaf.
functions: Hold the two face skins apart
Reduce face-skin buckling
Provide lightweight distributed support without acting as a hardware fixing block

cad.pattern: Repeated cellular field between leaf faces, interrupted at perimeter and hardware blocks
cad.placement: Inside a hollow-core flush leaf
cad.opening: Excluded around documented cut-outs and reinforcement
cad.load: Stabilises skins but is not assumed to anchor hardware

notes: A future low-detail model may represent the field symbolically while retaining the correct core type and excluded zones.

objects.name: flush door leaf perimeter frame
objects.definition: The concealed timber or engineered-wood edge frame around a hollow or composite flush door leaf, bonding the faces and forming reinforced leaf edges.
functions: Join and support the leaf faces at the perimeter
Provide edge strength
Receive compatible hinges, guides or lippings in documented zones

cad.pattern: Four concealed edge members surrounding the leaf core field
cad.placement: Between the face skins at leaf edges
cad.opening: Interrupted or reinforced at selected cut-outs
cad.load: Transfers face and local hardware loads around the leaf perimeter

notes: The concealed perimeter frame is not the stationary frame fixed into the wall.

objects.name: flush door leaf face skin
objects.definition: A thin continuous sheet bonded to one face of a flush internal door leaf over its core and perimeter frame.
functions: Form the visible broad face of the leaf
Stabilise the core assembly
Receive the selected decorative coating, laminate or veneer

cad.pattern: One broad sheet on each face of a flush leaf
cad.placement: Bonded over the core and perimeter frame
cad.opening: Trimmed around documented glazing and hardware openings
cad.load: Acts with the core assembly; not treated as an independently supported wall sheet

notes: A moulded face skin can create a panelled appearance without separate joinery panels.

objects.name: internal door leaf lock block
objects.definition: A local solid reinforcement concealed inside a lightweight door leaf near the closing edge to receive a compatible latch, lock or furniture fixing preparation.
functions: Provide material for latch and handle fixings
Reinforce the leaf around bored or morticed hardware
Define a limited hardware installation zone

cad.pattern: One local reinforced block at the nominated lock edge, sometimes handed
cad.placement: Inside a hollow-core leaf behind the handle and latch zone
cad.start: Specified height below the leaf top
cad.end: Specified height above the leaf bottom
cad.opening: Receives selected bore and edge drillings
cad.load: Transfers hardware loads into the leaf perimeter and faces

notes: Its side and extent are product-specific; the tool must not assume both leaf edges contain a full-height block.

objects.name: internal door leaf edge lipping
objects.definition: A narrow solid edge strip bonded to a door leaf to finish, protect or locally strengthen an exposed leaf edge and permit documented trimming or hardware preparation.
functions: Protect and finish the leaf edge
Provide local solid material for machining where allowed
Conceal the face-skin and core junction

cad.pattern: Narrow strip along selected vertical or horizontal leaf edges
cad.placement: At the exposed perimeter of a composite door leaf
cad.opening: Locally machined only as documented
cad.load: Provides edge protection and local fixing support, not the complete leaf load path

notes: Lipping depth and permitted trimming are selected-product facts, not generic constants.

objects.name: glazed internal door leaf
objects.definition: An internal door leaf containing one or more openings fitted with glass and its separate retention and glazing materials.
functions: Close an internal opening while admitting light or view
Support glass within the moving leaf
Coordinate leaf members, glazing beads, seals and safety-glazing evidence

cad.pattern: Door leaf containing one or more framed glazing apertures
cad.placement: Internal doorway where the selected glass and leaf are suitable
cad.opening: Each glazing aperture retains a selected pane and bead or gasket system
cad.load: Combined leaf and glass mass passes to compatible movement hardware

notes: Glass type and human-impact safety status are selected evidence; they are not inferred from transparency.

objects.name: internal door leaf glazing aperture
objects.definition: A prepared opening through an internal door leaf that is framed and sized to receive a glass pane with its retention and clearance system.
functions: Create the geometric opening for door glazing
Define the pane and bead boundary
Keep removed leaf material distinct from the installed glass
materials: void bounded by timber or composite leaf members

cad.pattern: One explicit cut-out per selected glazed panel
cad.placement: Within the door leaf clear of incompatible hardware zones
cad.opening: The object is the opening and hosts glass plus retention
cad.load: No material load; surrounding leaf members carry glass retention loads

notes: A cut-out is not glass and is excluded from material take-off except as a machining operation.

objects.name: louvred internal door leaf
objects.definition: An internal door leaf containing a field of angled or profiled blades held within a leaf frame to permit a selected degree of air and visual passage.
functions: Close the opening while allowing designed transfer through the blade field
Support repeated louvre blades
Coordinate privacy, airflow and hardware with the selected product

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel blades within one or more framed leaf fields
cad.placement: Internal doorway or cupboard opening selected for a louvred leaf
cad.opening: Open paths occur between blades
cad.load: Blade loads pass into the surrounding leaf frame; the leaf load passes to movement hardware

notes: Do not count a louvred leaf as a compliant ventilation opening without the applicable project calculation and operating assumptions.

objects.name: internal door louvre blade
objects.definition: One repeated angled or profiled slat spanning a louvred door-leaf opening and fixed into the surrounding leaf frame or blade carriers.
functions: Interrupt direct sight through the leaf
Leave a controlled passage between neighbouring blades
Transfer its own weight to the leaf frame

cad.pattern: Parallel repeated members at the selected blade pitch
cad.placement: Across a louvred field in the door leaf
cad.opening: Gap to neighbouring blade forms the transfer path
cad.load: Supported at blade ends by the leaf frame or carrier

notes: Free area depends on the complete blade geometry and cannot be inferred from leaf outline alone.

objects.name: double internal swing-door meeting assembly
objects.definition: The meeting-edge arrangement of two hinged internal door leaves, including active and inactive leaf roles, clearances, overlap or astragal and any coordinating bolts or latches.
functions: Close a wide opening with two swing leaves
Control the joint between leaves
Coordinate inactive-leaf restraint and active-leaf latching

cad.pattern: Two leaves sharing one frame and meeting at the centre of the opening
cad.placement: Wide internal swing doorway
cad.opening: Swing arcs and meeting clearance remain explicit
cad.load: Each leaf transfers separately to its hinge jamb; meeting hardware is not a vertical support

notes: Active and inactive leaf hardware must be modelled as roles, not assumed from equal leaf geometry.

objects.name: internal double-door astragal
objects.definition: A vertical strip fixed to or formed at the meeting edge of one leaf in a door pair to cover, rebate or seal the joint between the two leaves.
functions: Cover the meeting-edge gap
Provide a closing face for the opposite leaf
Carry a selected seal or strike where designed

cad.pattern: One vertical strip along the selected meeting edge
cad.placement: On the active or inactive leaf as documented
cad.opening: Overlaps the meeting clearance without filling the swing path
cad.load: Moves with and is supported by its host leaf

notes: Astragal location and sequence affect which leaf must close first.

objects.name: internal door frame and trim assembly
objects.definition: The fixed internal doorway frame, packers, fixings, stop or rebate and its room-side architrave or flush-finish lining junctions.
functions: Define the finished doorway opening
Support hinges, strikes, tracks or pivots
Bridge or finish the junction between wall lining and frame

cad.pattern: Two jambs and a head around the opening with explicit wall packing, fixings and side-specific trim
cad.placement: Fixed inside an internal wall opening
cad.start: Finished floor or nominated sill level
cad.opening: Contains the operable doorway opening
cad.load: Transfers leaf and hardware loads through fixings and packers into supporting wall members

notes: Architrave and flush-finish square-set details are alternative lining junctions, not compulsory parts of every frame.

objects.name: timber internal door jamb set
objects.definition: A timber frame set made from two vertical jambs and a head, usually supplied with a rebate or separate stop and fixed into the wall opening with packers and fasteners.
functions: Form the fixed opening around an internal leaf
Receive hinges, strike and stops
Provide an edge for architrave or lining junctions

cad.pattern: U-shaped head-and-jamb frame fitted to one wall opening
cad.placement: Between the finished wall faces at an internal doorway
cad.opening: Inner faces define leaf clearances and opening
cad.load: Transfers leaf and latch loads through packers and fixings to wall framing

notes: Jamb set is the fixed timber frame; architraves are separate trims fitted after packing and fixing.

objects.name: rebated internal door jamb set
objects.definition: An internal door jamb set whose head and jamb profiles include an integral step or rebate against which the closed leaf bears.
functions: Provide an integral closing stop
Locate the closed leaf in the frame
Receive compatible seals or strike preparation where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous rebated profile around both jambs and head as selected
cad.placement: Fixed around the internal door opening
cad.end: Across head and down opposite jamb
cad.opening: Rebate bounds the closed-leaf position
cad.load: Frame transfers leaf loads through wall fixings; rebate receives closing contact only

notes: The integral rebate replaces a separate planted stop only where the selected frame profile is designed that way.

objects.name: split internal door jamb set
objects.definition: An adjustable internal door frame made from overlapping or interlocking jamb halves that wrap the finished wall thickness and are assembled around the opening.
functions: Accommodate a range of finished wall thicknesses
Provide a framed and trimmed opening from two matching sides
Conceal the wall edge within the frame profile

cad.pattern: Paired profiles wrapping each side of the wall at both jambs and head
cad.placement: Around a completed or measured internal wall opening
cad.opening: Inner stop or rebate defines the closed-leaf position
cad.load: Movement hardware loads must transfer into suitable wall support, not only the overlapping trim

notes: This split jamb wraps wall thickness; it is not the split stud that forms the pocket of a cavity slider.

objects.name: flush-finish steel internal door frame
objects.definition: A formed steel internal door frame with perforated or prepared side flanges finished into the wall lining so the opening can be completed without conventional face architraves.
functions: Form an internal door opening with a minimal flush wall junction
Receive hinges and strike hardware
Provide a plaster-finished edge instead of applied architrave

cad.pattern: Formed head and jamb sections with lining-facing flanges embedded into the finish
cad.placement: Fixed to supported wall jambs and head before final lining finishing
cad.end: Across the head and down the opposite side
cad.opening: Rebate and clearances define the operable opening
cad.load: Transfers leaf loads through frame fixings and packers into wall framing

notes: Frameless is an appearance term: a physical steel frame is still present and must be drawn.

objects.name: flush door-frame finishing flange
objects.definition: A perforated or textured flange along a flush-finish metal door frame that is fixed over the lining edge and embedded in the jointing finish.
functions: Anchor the frame edge to the lining and wall support
Provide a keyed surface for jointing compound
Create a straight flush transition from wall face to door reveal

cad.pattern: Continuous perforated flange along both jambs and head
cad.placement: Over or beside the wall lining at the frame perimeter
cad.opening: Stops at the inner reveal edge
cad.load: Stabilises the frame-to-lining edge; principal leaf load transfers to wall framing

notes: The flange becomes visually concealed but remains a physical section under the finished wall surface.

objects.name: flush door-frame latch-plate insert
objects.definition: A prepared metal insert or reinforced recess in a flush-finish door frame that receives and positions the selected latch strike plate.
functions: Provide a stable strike fixing zone
Locate the latch bolt relative to the leaf
Protect the thin formed frame around the strike preparation

cad.pattern: One insert at the selected latch height on the closing jamb
cad.placement: Within or behind the formed frame strike preparation
cad.opening: Aligns with latch-bolt entry
cad.load: Transfers latch impact and holding loads into the frame

notes: The insert supports the strike; it is not the removable strike plate itself.

objects.name: internal door architrave set
objects.definition: The room-side trim around an internal door opening, normally formed by two jamb pieces and one head piece that cover the frame-to-wall lining junction.
functions: Cover packers, fixings and the lining-to-frame gap
Create a finished border around the opening
Remain separately measurable from jamb and wall lining

cad.pattern: Three trim pieces around each trimmed face of the opening
cad.placement: Over the frame-to-lining junction on one or both wall faces
cad.end: Up jamb, across head and down opposite jamb
cad.opening: Borders but does not reduce the inner frame opening unless designed to
cad.load: Non-structural finish fixed to jamb and wall edge

notes: Architrave is an attachment to the wall and frame, not part of the wall lining material itself.

objects.name: internal door architrave head piece
objects.definition: The horizontal architrave member across the top of an internal door frame, joined to the two vertical architrave pieces.
functions: Cover the head-frame to wall-lining junction
Complete the visible trim border
Join the two jamb architraves

cad.pattern: One horizontal trim length per trimmed frame face
cad.placement: Across the top of the frame and lining junction
cad.opening: Borders the frame head
cad.load: Non-structural finish fixed to the head and wall edge

notes: The trim head and structural wall opening head are different objects.

objects.name: internal door architrave jamb piece
objects.definition: One vertical architrave member beside an internal door frame, covering the jamb-to-wall lining junction from floor or skirting to the head trim.
functions: Cover the jamb packing and lining edge
Form the vertical side of the opening trim
Meet skirting and head architrave cleanly

cad.pattern: Two vertical trim lengths per trimmed frame face
cad.placement: Along each jamb-to-lining junction
cad.opening: Borders the jamb reveal
cad.load: Non-structural finish fixed to jamb and wall edge

notes: A tool should coordinate the jamb architrave with the skirting termination rather than merge them into one member.

objects.name: cavity-slider square-set reveal trim
objects.definition: A formed trim section used at a cavity-slider opening to finish the lining directly into the split or closing jamb zone without applied timber architrave.
functions: Create a clean lining edge around a cavity-slider opening
Replace selected timber architrave or closing-jamb trim
Provide a jointing edge for the wall finish

cad.pattern: Continuous trim lengths around the selected cavity-slider opening edges
cad.placement: At the wall-lining termination beside the door pocket and closing side
cad.end: Across head and down opposite side where applicable
cad.opening: Defines the finished reveal without obstructing the leaf path
cad.load: Finishing section only; track and leaf loads pass to the cavity frame and wall structure

notes: Square set describes the visual lining finish; the physical reveal section and supporting pocket frame still exist.

objects.name: internal door hardware system
objects.definition: The coordinated movement, operating, latching, locking, stopping and closing hardware fitted to an internal door leaf and frame.
functions: Support and guide the leaf
Allow a person to operate and secure the door
Control open and closed positions without treating hardware ratings as geometry

cad.pattern: Discrete hardware fitted at documented positions on leaf, frame, wall, floor or track
cad.placement: At movement axes, operating height, closing edges and open-position control points
cad.end: Supported, latched, locked, stopped or controlled leaf state
cad.opening: Hardware must preserve intended opening and movement clearances
cad.load: Transfers leaf, user, impact and holding loads into compatible leaf, frame, wall or floor substrates

notes: Hardware sets must be compatible with leaf construction, frame, mass, handing and any fire or access requirements.

objects.name: internal door butt hinge
objects.definition: A two-leaf hinge with a central pin, morticed or surface-fixed at the edge of a swing door leaf and its jamb to form the rotation axis.
functions: Support the swing leaf
Create a fixed rotation axis
Transfer leaf weight and operating loads to the jamb

cad.pattern: Two or more hinges aligned on one vertical swing axis
cad.placement: Between hinge edge of leaf and hinge jamb
cad.opening: Knuckle clearance permits the selected swing
cad.load: Transfers vertical leaf weight and horizontal operating loads into the jamb

notes: Quantity and rating depend on selected leaf mass, size, closer, usage and frame, not a universal hinge count.

objects.name: loose-pin internal door butt hinge
objects.definition: A butt hinge whose removable pin allows the two hinge leaves and the door leaf to be separated without removing the hinge screws.
functions: Support ordinary swing-door movement
Permit convenient leaf removal when accessible
Retain the hinge leaves on leaf and jamb during removal

cad.pattern: Aligned hinges with a separately removable axial pin
cad.placement: Between leaf and hinge jamb with pin access maintained
cad.opening: Pin removal requires accessible clearance
cad.load: Carries leaf loads while pin is installed

notes: A loose pin can aid removal but does not by itself prove the NCC sanitary-compartment readily removable arrangement.

objects.name: fixed-pin internal door butt hinge
objects.definition: A butt hinge with a pin retained against normal removal, keeping both hinge leaves permanently connected during ordinary use.
functions: Support swing-door movement
Resist unintended pin removal
Transfer leaf loads through a retained hinge axis

cad.pattern: Aligned fixed-axis hinges between leaf and jamb
cad.placement: At the swing edge of the leaf
cad.opening: Knuckle clears frame throughout swing
cad.load: Transfers leaf weight and operating load into jamb

notes: Pin retention affects removal and security but does not establish hinge load capacity.

objects.name: concealed internal door hinge
objects.definition: A multi-link or pivoting hinge recessed into the door edge and frame so most or all of the hinge is hidden when the leaf is closed.
functions: Support and pivot a swing door
Hide the hinge body in the closed position
Allow selected three-dimensional alignment where the product provides it

cad.pattern: Two or more concealed bodies aligned on the swing axis
cad.placement: Recessed into compatible leaf edge and jamb
cad.opening: Linkage envelope must clear the reveal throughout swing
cad.load: Transfers leaf weight through concealed links and fixings into jamb support

notes: The leaf and frame need compatible solid fixing zones and mortices; concealment is not merely a visual setting.

objects.name: butt-hinge leaf plate
objects.definition: One of the two flat plates of a butt hinge, containing screw holes and rolled knuckles and fixed to either the door leaf or the jamb.
functions: Fix one side of the hinge to its substrate
Form alternating knuckles around the pin
Transfer load between screws and the hinge axis

cad.pattern: Two plates per butt hinge
cad.placement: Morticed or surface-fixed to leaf edge and jamb
cad.opening: Screw holes and countersinks remain explicit at detailed LOD
cad.load: Transfers hinge forces between pin and fixing screws

notes: Door leaf and hinge leaf are different objects despite sharing the word leaf.

objects.name: butt-hinge pin
objects.definition: The axial metal pin passing through the interleaved knuckles of a butt hinge to connect its two leaves and form the rotation axis.
functions: Join the hinge leaves
Define the rotation axis
Carry shear and bearing forces between hinge knuckles

cad.pattern: One axial pin per butt hinge
cad.placement: Through aligned hinge knuckles
cad.opening: Requires removal clearance only for loose-pin types
cad.load: Carries hinge shear and bearing between leaves

notes: Pin removability is a hardware attribute and can affect door-recovery arrangements.

objects.name: internal door hinge screw
objects.definition: A screw fixing a hinge leaf plate to the door leaf or frame through its countersunk or prepared holes.
functions: Clamp the hinge plate to the substrate
Transfer hinge shear and withdrawal forces
Keep the plate seated in its mortice or on its fixing face

cad.pattern: Repeated through each hinge-plate fixing hole
cad.placement: From hinge plate into leaf reinforcement or jamb support
cad.opening: Uses prepared pilot or fixing hole
cad.load: Transfers hinge forces into compatible solid substrate

notes: Screw length and substrate suitability are selected-system data, especially for heavy or solid-core leaves.

objects.name: internal door pivot set
objects.definition: A top-and-bottom pivot hardware pair supporting a swing door about an axis offset or aligned near its edge instead of using conventional side butt hinges.
functions: Support the leaf at top and bottom pivot points
Create the selected swing axis
Allow large or special internal leaves where the complete system is designed for them

cad.pattern: One aligned top and bottom pivot pair per leaf
cad.placement: Between leaf top and head support and between leaf bottom and floor or sill support
cad.opening: Leaf sweeps on the selected pivot axis with heel and leading-edge clearance
cad.load: Most vertical load passes through the bottom pivot; top pivot restrains and guides as designed

notes: The supporting floor and head must be verified; a pivot symbol alone does not prove capacity.

objects.name: internal passage latchset
objects.definition: A non-locking internal door furniture set with handles or knobs, spindle, spring latch, faceplate, strike, fixings and trims for a freely operable passage door.
functions: Retract the latch from either side
Hold the closed leaf against its stop
Provide ordinary non-locking operation between rooms

cad.pattern: Paired handles through the leaf, one edge latch and one matching jamb strike
cad.placement: At selected operating height on the closing edge of a swing leaf
cad.opening: Bore, cross-bore and strike recess follow selected hardware
cad.load: User torque and latch impact transfer into lock block, leaf edge and closing jamb

notes: Passage describes function, not handle shape or accessibility compliance.

objects.name: internal privacy latchset
objects.definition: An internal latchset with inside privacy control and an outside emergency-release provision, typically used for a bathroom, ensuite or bedroom where keyed security is not intended.
functions: Latch the closed leaf
Allow privacy locking from the inside
Allow emergency release from the outside using the selected mechanism
not_synonyms: sanitary door recovery arrangement by itself

cad.pattern: Paired furniture with inside privacy control, outside release, edge latch and jamb strike
cad.placement: At selected operating height on a privacy-room door
cad.start: Inside privacy action or normal handle operation
cad.opening: Leaf and frame preparations follow selected set
cad.load: Operating and latch loads pass into leaf reinforcement and strike jamb

notes: Emergency release hardware supports access to the latch; occupant recovery may also require outward opening, sliding, removability or the specified internal clearance.

objects.name: internal dummy door furniture set
objects.definition: A fixed handle or knob set attached to a door leaf without a spindle-operated latch, used as a pull or to match nearby operating furniture.
functions: Provide a handhold for pushing or pulling
Match the appearance of operating furniture
Avoid implying a latch where none is installed
not_synonyms: inactive handle that still operates a latch

cad.pattern: One or two fixed furniture pieces without a latch spindle
cad.placement: On cupboard, wardrobe, inactive or roller-latched leaf as selected
cad.end: Leaf moves through another holding mechanism or no latch
cad.opening: Only fixing holes, not a latch edge bore unless separately required
cad.load: Pull load transfers through fixings into leaf reinforcement

notes: Dummy refers to non-operating latch function, not a temporary or decorative-only model object.

objects.name: keyed internal door lockset
objects.definition: A door lockset used at an internal or interconnecting doorway with a key-operated outside function and compatible inside control, latch or bolt, strike and furniture.
functions: Latch and secure a selected internal or interconnecting door
Permit controlled keyed access
Coordinate cylinder, lock body, furniture and strike

cad.pattern: Keyed furniture and lock body through or within the leaf with a matching frame strike
cad.placement: On selected internal security or garage-interconnection doors
cad.end: Latch or bolt held by strike
cad.opening: Requires selected face, edge and frame preparations
cad.load: Operating and holding loads transfer into leaf reinforcement and supported strike jamb

notes: Function and security rating are selected-product evidence; keyed does not mean suitable for every fire, egress or access path.

objects.name: internal door lever handle
objects.definition: A projecting lever gripped or pressed by the user and connected through a spindle or lock mechanism to operate an internal door latch or lock.
functions: Provide a hand-operated input
Rotate the spindle or mechanism
Return to its resting position through the selected spring arrangement

cad.pattern: One handle on each operated side of the leaf unless function differs
cad.placement: At selected operating height on the door face
cad.opening: Projects clear of leaf face and frame during operation
cad.load: User force passes through rose or plate and spindle into latch mechanism

notes: Lever shape alone does not establish AS 1428.1 compliance; clearance, return, force, height and the applicable path must be checked.

objects.name: internal door knob
objects.definition: A rounded or shaped rotary grip connected to a spindle or lock mechanism to operate an internal door latch or lock.
functions: Provide a rotary hand grip
Turn the spindle or lock follower
Return through the selected spring arrangement

cad.pattern: One knob on each operated leaf side unless function differs
cad.placement: At selected operating height on the door face
cad.opening: Projects from the leaf face through its operating arc
cad.load: User torque passes through spindle into latch or lock

notes: A rotary knob may be unsuitable for a required accessible path even though it is ordinary residential hardware.

objects.name: internal door handle rose
objects.definition: A round, square or shaped trim and mounting piece surrounding the spindle at the base of a door lever or knob on the leaf face.
functions: Cover handle fixings and leaf preparation
Support or locate the handle bearing and return hardware
Provide the visible interface between handle and leaf

cad.pattern: One rose beneath each lever or knob
cad.placement: Against the leaf face around the spindle hole
cad.opening: Covers the central preparation and fixings
cad.load: Distributes handle fixing and bearing loads into the leaf

notes: A rose is compact furniture; a backplate is an elongated plate and remains a separate option.

objects.name: internal door handle backplate
objects.definition: An elongated plate mounted behind a door lever or knob, often also carrying a keyhole, turn, cylinder or privacy control opening.
functions: Mount and trim operating furniture
Cover a larger leaf preparation area
Align handle and lock-control functions on one plate

cad.pattern: One plate on each required leaf face
cad.placement: At the handle and lock preparation
cad.opening: Covers handle, cylinder or turn holes
cad.load: Distributes furniture fixing loads into the leaf

notes: Rose and backplate are alternative furniture mounting forms, although some sets combine separate roses and escutcheons.

objects.name: internal door handle spindle
objects.definition: A square or profiled bar passing through the door leaf and latch or lock follower to connect operating handles on opposite sides.
functions: Transmit handle rotation
Synchronise the two operating sides where required
Turn the latch or lock follower

cad.pattern: One transverse bar through the latch or lock follower
cad.placement: Across the leaf thickness between inside and outside handles
cad.opening: Passes through leaf and mechanism preparation
cad.load: Carries operating torque between handles and follower

notes: Some privacy and lock functions use split or separate spindles; the tool must follow the selected set.

objects.name: internal door tubular latch
objects.definition: A compact cylindrical or tubular spring-latch mechanism inserted from the door edge and operated by a transverse spindle through the leaf.
functions: Project a spring latch bolt into the frame strike
Retract the bolt when the handle turns
Hold the leaf closed without a separate deadbolt

cad.pattern: One edge-inserted mechanism per latching leaf
cad.placement: Within the closing edge at handle height
cad.opening: Requires edge bore and transverse spindle bore
cad.load: Latch impact and holding load transfer through faceplate and case into the leaf edge

notes: Tubular describes the compact case and preparation, not the handle or privacy function.

objects.name: internal door spring latch bolt
objects.definition: The bevelled or shaped spring-loaded bolt that projects from a latch case into the frame strike and retracts when the handle operates.
functions: Engage the strike as the door closes
Hold the leaf at the closed position
Retract against its spring for opening

cad.pattern: One moving bolt at the latch case end
cad.placement: Projects from leaf edge toward the closing jamb
cad.opening: Moves through the faceplate aperture
cad.load: Carries closing impact and closed-position holding force

notes: Latch bolt and deadbolt have different operating and holding functions.

objects.name: internal door latch faceplate
objects.definition: A small plate fixed to the door edge around the projecting latch bolt, covering the latch case entry and providing a finished fixing face.
functions: Retain and trim the latch case at the leaf edge
Provide a smooth edge surface around the bolt
Carry latch fixing screws

cad.pattern: One plate over the edge-latch preparation
cad.placement: Flush or surface-fixed on the leaf closing edge
cad.opening: Contains the latch-bolt aperture
cad.load: Retains the latch case and carries local edge fixing loads

notes: The faceplate is on the moving leaf; the strike plate is on the fixed frame.

objects.name: internal door latch strike plate
objects.definition: A metal plate fixed to the closing jamb with an opening that receives the latch bolt and a lip or shaped edge that guides it as the leaf closes.
functions: Receive the projected latch bolt
Protect the jamb from repeated latch contact
Transfer closed-door holding loads into the frame

cad.pattern: One strike aligned with each latch or compatible bolt
cad.placement: On the closing jamb opposite the leaf latch
cad.opening: Receives the latch bolt and may open into a dust box
cad.load: Transfers latch impact and holding force through screws and jamb into wall support

notes: An electric strike is a separate powered release device and must not be substituted by changing an attribute on a passive strike.

objects.name: internal door strike dust box
objects.definition: A small recessed box behind a latch or bolt strike opening that closes the jamb cavity and receives the projected bolt.
functions: Provide a clean enclosed bolt pocket
Keep debris and exposed substrate away from the moving bolt
Finish the recess behind the strike plate

cad.pattern: One recessed pocket behind a boxed strike
cad.placement: Within the closing jamb behind the strike opening
cad.opening: Receives latch or bolt projection
cad.load: Normally a lining and debris-control component; primary holding load passes through the strike plate and jamb

notes: Some timber-jamb installations omit a separate box; model it only when the selected hardware includes one.

objects.name: internal door privacy turn
objects.definition: An inside thumbturn, snib, button or similar control used to engage and release the privacy function of an internal lock or latchset.
functions: Engage privacy locking from inside
Release privacy locking from inside
Show or coordinate occupied status where the selected set provides it

cad.pattern: One inside privacy control per privacy set
cad.placement: On the room side of leaf furniture
cad.end: Privacy actuator in latch or lock
cad.opening: Uses selected spindle or preparation through furniture
cad.load: Transmits light user torque or push force to the privacy mechanism

notes: The matching outside release is separately modelled in health and amenity because its occupant-recovery role is not ordinary privacy hardware alone.

objects.name: internal door mortice lock body
objects.definition: A rectangular lock case recessed into the edge of a door leaf and containing the latch, bolt, followers, springs and key or turn mechanisms for the selected function.
functions: Contain the door locking mechanism
Operate a latch, deadbolt or both
Connect furniture, cylinder or turns to the edge bolts

cad.pattern: One recessed case at the leaf closing edge
cad.placement: Within a documented mortice in a solid or reinforced leaf edge
cad.end: Latch or bolt at leaf edge
cad.opening: Requires edge mortice and transverse preparations
cad.load: Transfers operating and holding loads into the reinforced leaf edge

notes: A lightweight leaf needs the documented reinforcement and preparation for the selected mortice case.

objects.name: internal door lock cylinder
objects.definition: A keyed removable or integrated cylinder that accepts the authorised key and drives the locking mechanism of an internal or interconnecting door lock.
functions: Recognise the mechanical key
Rotate a cam or tailpiece
Control the keyed side of the lock function

cad.pattern: One or two cylinder faces aligned with the lock body
cad.placement: Through furniture and leaf into the lock mechanism
cad.opening: Requires selected cylinder cut-out and retention
cad.load: Transmits key torque to the lock mechanism

notes: Cylinder format and keying are hardware data; a generic round hole does not define them.

objects.name: internal door lock escutcheon
objects.definition: A small trim plate or rose surrounding a keyhole, cylinder or privacy control on the face of a door leaf.
functions: Finish and protect the leaf preparation
Locate or cover the cylinder or key opening
Match adjacent handle furniture

cad.pattern: One trim at each exposed key, cylinder or turn opening
cad.placement: Against the leaf face around the lock control
cad.opening: Covers the preparation edge without obstructing operation
cad.load: Light trim and protective loads only

notes: Escutcheon can be separate from handle furniture or incorporated into a backplate.

objects.name: internal door deadbolt
objects.definition: A positive locking bolt moved by a key or turn rather than by spring action, projecting from the door edge into a matching strike when locked.
functions: Secure the closed leaf
Provide positive bolt engagement
Remain projected until deliberately retracted

cad.pattern: One positive bolt aligned with its strike
cad.placement: Within the leaf closing edge or a dedicated lock case
cad.opening: Moves through a forend aperture into the strike
cad.load: Carries holding and forced-entry loads into leaf and jamb support

notes: A deadbolt is not spring-latched and may have egress implications depending on its location and function.

objects.name: inactive-leaf flush bolt
objects.definition: A recessed sliding bolt in the edge or face of an inactive door leaf that engages the frame head, floor or threshold to hold that leaf closed.
functions: Restrain the inactive leaf of a door pair
Provide a stable strike for the active leaf arrangement
Retract to allow the full opening to be used

cad.pattern: Top, bottom or paired bolts on the inactive meeting stile
cad.placement: Recessed into the inactive leaf edge and aligned to head or floor strike
cad.opening: Bolt retracts within the leaf before opening
cad.load: Transfers holding loads from inactive leaf into frame head or floor support

notes: Floor engagement must coordinate with finishes and any step-free doorway requirements.

objects.name: internal door open-position stop assembly
objects.definition: A wall-, floor- or frame-mounted fitting that limits the open movement of an internal swing door and protects the leaf, handle, wall or nearby objects from impact.
functions: Limit the swing angle
Receive opening impact
Protect adjacent finishes and hardware

cad.pattern: One stop at the designed open position per swing leaf where required
cad.placement: On wall, floor, skirting or frame aligned with a robust leaf contact point
cad.opening: Defines maximum swing without blocking required circulation
cad.load: Transfers impact through its fixing into a suitable substrate

notes: The open-position stop is different from the fixed jamb stop moulding that locates the leaf when closed.

objects.name: wall-mounted internal door stop
objects.definition: A projecting stop fixed to a wall, skirting or joinery face and positioned to receive the door leaf or handle at its intended maximum swing.
functions: Limit door swing
Keep handle or leaf from striking the wall
Transfer impact into the wall fixing point

cad.pattern: One projecting stop aligned with the open leaf or handle
cad.placement: On a supported wall or skirting surface behind the opening door
cad.opening: Sits at the selected swing limit
cad.load: Transfers opening impact into wall backing or stud

notes: Fixing only to unsupported plasterboard may not carry repeated impact.

objects.name: floor-mounted internal door stop
objects.definition: A low stop fixed to the floor and positioned to contact the door leaf at its intended maximum opening angle.
functions: Limit door swing where a wall stop is unsuitable
Receive impact at a robust lower leaf point
Keep the leaf or handle clear of adjacent construction

cad.pattern: One low stop at the selected open-leaf position
cad.placement: On finished floor clear of circulation and concealed services
cad.opening: Defines maximum swing and remains a trip or access consideration
cad.load: Transfers impact into the verified floor substrate

notes: Coordinate penetrations with waterproofing, underfloor services and step-free circulation.

objects.name: magnetic internal door stop and holder
objects.definition: A two-part door stop with a floor- or wall-mounted magnetic catch and a matching leaf plate that limits swing and can retain the door in the open position.
functions: Stop the opening leaf
Hold the leaf open using magnetic attraction
Release when sufficient closing force is applied

cad.pattern: One fixed magnetic body aligned with one leaf-mounted keeper
cad.placement: At the selected open position on wall or floor and matching leaf face
cad.opening: Holds the leaf at maximum selected swing
cad.load: Impact and holding loads divide between fixed substrate and leaf fixings

notes: Do not use a simple magnetic holder where a fire doorset must self-close unless the complete approved release arrangement permits it.

objects.name: controlled internal door closer assembly
objects.definition: A mechanical closer with a spring and damping mechanism connected between an internal swing leaf and its frame to return the opened leaf toward the closed position at a controlled speed.
functions: Store energy during opening
Return the leaf toward closed
Control closing and final latching speed using the selected mechanism

cad.pattern: One closer body plus linkage per controlled swing leaf
cad.placement: On leaf and frame head or concealed in a compatible frame, leaf or floor
cad.end: Controlled return brings latch to strike
cad.opening: Closer and arm sweep must clear frame and adjacent construction
cad.load: Opening and closing forces pass through closer fixings into reinforced leaf and frame

notes: The fire-safety object represents a closer used in a protected-opening system. This ordinary object does not inherit that compliance role.

objects.name: surface-mounted door closer body
objects.definition: The visible surface-mounted housing containing the spring, piston, hydraulic damping and adjustment parts of a controlled door closer.
functions: Store closing energy
Damp closing movement
Provide selected adjustment and arm connection

cad.pattern: One rectangular closer body per controlled leaf
cad.placement: On leaf face or frame head according to selected mounting
cad.opening: Body clears frame and ceiling during full swing
cad.load: Transfers spring and damping reactions through mounting screws into reinforced substrate

notes: Mounting position changes the arm geometry and available force; it is not a cosmetic relocation.

objects.name: door closer articulated arm
objects.definition: A jointed metal linkage connecting a surface closer spindle to the leaf or frame shoe and transmitting movement between the door and closer body.
functions: Transmit leaf rotation to the closer spindle
Return closer torque to the leaf
Accommodate the selected mounting geometry through an articulated joint

cad.pattern: One articulated linkage between closer spindle and fixing shoe
cad.placement: Across the top of the leaf and frame
cad.opening: Sweeps through a changing linkage envelope
cad.load: Carries closer torque and door reaction between body and leaf or frame

notes: Arm and slide-channel closers use different geometry and should not share one adjustable shape.

objects.name: door closer slide rail
objects.definition: A linear channel containing a sliding block connected to a closer arm, used in place of a projecting articulated-arm shoe arrangement.
functions: Guide the closer arm connection along a fixed line
Transmit closer force between frame and leaf
Reduce the projecting linkage envelope

cad.pattern: One straight rail with a moving slider per closer
cad.placement: Along frame head or leaf top face
cad.opening: Slider travels within channel as leaf swings
cad.load: Transfers closer force through rail fixings into supported frame or leaf

notes: This is a closer component, not the head track that supports a sliding door leaf.

objects.name: surface-sliding internal door hardware assembly
objects.definition: The track, rollers or hangers, wall spacers or brackets, stops, anti-jump restraints, floor guide, pulls and optional cover used to move an internal door leaf across the face of a wall.
functions: Suspend and guide the sliding leaf outside the wall cavity
Limit travel and prevent derailment
Transfer leaf weight into the supported track and wall

cad.pattern: One supported horizontal track with two or more hangers, end stops and a lower guide per leaf
cad.placement: On the wall face above and beside the doorway opening
cad.end: Open parked position along the wall
cad.opening: Leaf overlaps the opening and needs clear wall travel
cad.load: Leaf weight transfers through rollers, track and brackets into wall studs, lintel or designed support

notes: Wall linings and a decorative batten alone are not verified track support.

objects.name: surface-sliding door track bracket
objects.definition: A structural bracket or rest plate fixing the surface-sliding door track to the wall support and holding it at the required offset from the wall face.
functions: Support the track
Set the wall clearance
Transfer vertical and horizontal roller loads into the wall

cad.pattern: Repeated brackets at documented support points along the track
cad.placement: Between track and supported wall framing or backing
cad.opening: Keeps track clear of architrave, lining and leaf thickness
cad.load: Transfers track reactions into designed wall support

notes: Bracket spacing and fixing capacity follow the selected system and leaf mass.

objects.name: surface-sliding door track wall spacer
objects.definition: A discrete spacer between a surface-sliding track or bracket and the wall, maintaining clearance for the leaf, architrave and hardware.
functions: Set track stand-off from the wall
Keep the moving leaf clear of finishes
Provide a controlled bearing path at fixing points

cad.pattern: One spacer at each selected track fixing
cad.placement: Between wall or backing and track fixing face
cad.opening: Maintains clearance over trim and leaf travel
cad.load: Carries compression and fixing shear as part of the documented support system

notes: A spacer sets offset but may not replace a load-rated bracket or solid wall backing.

objects.name: internal sliding-door track pelmet
objects.definition: A removable or fixed cover enclosing or screening the visible head track and roller hardware of a surface or cavity sliding door.
functions: Conceal track and hangers
Provide a finished head line
Remain removable where hardware access is required

cad.pattern: One continuous cover along the visible track length
cad.placement: In front of, below or around the track without touching moving rollers
cad.opening: Allows required maintenance access and leaf clearance
cad.load: Decorative cover supported independently from the moving leaf

notes: A pelmet is trim and must not be mistaken for the structural track support.

objects.name: internal sliding-door track stop
objects.definition: A fixed resilient stop at a sliding-door track end or selected travel limit that contacts the hanger or leaf hardware and prevents over-travel.
functions: Limit sliding travel
Absorb end-of-travel impact
Keep rollers and leaf within the supported track range

cad.pattern: Stops at open and closed travel limits as required
cad.placement: Within or on the head track
cad.opening: Defines maximum travel without reducing intended clear opening
cad.load: Transfers end impact into track and its support

notes: Track stop and soft-close damper can coexist; neither should be omitted merely because travel is constrained in the model.

objects.name: surface-sliding door anti-jump fitting
objects.definition: A small restraint mounted to the sliding leaf or roller assembly that limits upward movement and helps prevent the roller leaving an exposed track.
functions: Limit leaf uplift
Reduce derailment risk
Maintain the roller-to-track relationship during impact or irregular operation

cad.pattern: One restraint near each exposed roller as documented
cad.placement: On top of the leaf or hanger close to the track
cad.end: Controlled clearance below or around track
cad.opening: Travels with the leaf without binding
cad.load: Carries exceptional uplift restraint, not normal vertical leaf weight

notes: Anti-jump hardware supplements the lower guide and does not replace it.

objects.name: surface-sliding internal door floor guide
objects.definition: A low fixed guide engaging a groove or the faces of a surface-sliding door leaf to restrain sideways movement while allowing horizontal travel.
functions: Keep the suspended leaf plumb
Limit transverse swing
Guide the leaf through its open and closed travel

cad.pattern: One low guide positioned so it remains engaged throughout travel
cad.placement: On the floor near the doorway or wall line
cad.opening: Does not project into required circulation more than the selected system
cad.load: Carries transverse guide forces; vertical leaf weight remains on head track

notes: Coordinate floor penetrations with waterproofing, services and floor finishes.

objects.name: internal sliding-door flush pull
objects.definition: A recessed hand pull set into the broad face of a sliding door leaf so it projects little or not at all beyond the leaf surface.
functions: Provide a grip for sliding the leaf
Allow the leaf face to pass close to a wall or enter a cavity
Finish the recessed leaf preparation

cad.pattern: One pull on each required leaf face
cad.placement: At selected operating height clear of leaf edges and cavity contact
cad.opening: Does not project beyond permitted cavity or wall clearance
cad.load: User pull load transfers through fixing or recessed cup into the leaf

notes: A face flush pull cannot retrieve a leaf fully parked inside a cavity without a separate edge pull or lock pull.

objects.name: internal sliding-door edge pull
objects.definition: A retractable or folding pull fitted into the closing edge of a sliding door leaf so a leaf parked inside a cavity can be drawn out.
functions: Provide a grip at the leaf edge
Retract flush when not in use
Retrieve the leaf from its pocket or close wall position

cad.pattern: One edge pull at accessible height on the closing edge
cad.placement: Recessed into the sliding leaf edge
cad.opening: Must retract within the leaf edge before entering the pocket
cad.load: User retrieval load transfers into reinforced leaf edge

notes: Some cavity locksets integrate an edge pull; do not model a duplicate separate pull unless both are selected.

objects.name: cavity-sliding internal door hardware assembly
objects.definition: The track, hangers, guide, stops, soft-close device, pulls and optional latch or lock hardware coordinating a door leaf that slides into a framed wall pocket.
functions: Suspend and guide the leaf into the wall cavity
Control travel and closing
Coordinate pocket clearances, retrieval and optional privacy or keyed functions

cad.pattern: One head track and hanger set guiding each leaf between closed opening and wall pocket
cad.placement: Within and above a cavity-slider pocket frame
cad.opening: Leaf and hardware maintain clearance from split studs, linings and fixings
cad.load: Leaf weight passes through hangers and track into the pocket-frame head and supported wall structure

notes: Wall fixings and services must stay clear of the moving leaf pocket.

objects.name: cavity-slider closing jamb
objects.definition: The fixed vertical jamb at the closing side of a cavity-slider opening, receiving the leaf edge and any strike, seal, rebate or recessed closing profile.
functions: Define the fully closed leaf position
Receive latch or lock strike hardware
Finish and cover the closing-side wall edge

cad.pattern: One vertical receiver at the side opposite the pocket
cad.placement: At the closing edge of the doorway opening
cad.opening: Leaf edge enters or contacts selected closing profile
cad.load: Receives latch and closing impact and transfers them into wall support

notes: A recessed closing jamb can reduce the visible closed-edge gap but remains distinct from the structural wall jamb stud.

objects.name: cavity-slider split-jamb lining member
objects.definition: One of the narrow finished vertical members at the mouth of a cavity-slider pocket, flanking the moving leaf while maintaining clearance into the pocket.
functions: Finish the pocket mouth
Guide the visual edge of the opening
Keep wall lining and trim clear of the moving leaf

cad.pattern: Paired narrow vertical trims at the pocket entrance
cad.placement: On both faces of the moving leaf at the pocket mouth
cad.opening: Maintains a clear slot into the wall pocket
cad.load: Trim and guide-contact loads only; structural pocket support comes from split studs and frame

notes: Split-jamb lining is visible trim; the existing split-stud object is the wall-pocket framing member.

objects.name: cavity sliding-door lock body
objects.definition: A compact lock or latch mechanism recessed into a cavity-sliding door leaf and arranged to operate within the limited clearance of the wall pocket.
functions: Provide passage, privacy or keyed locking function
Project a compatible bolt into the closing-jamb strike
Remain flush enough for the leaf to enter the pocket

cad.pattern: One recessed lock mechanism at the closing edge and selected operating height
cad.placement: Within a reinforced cavity-slider leaf
cad.start: Face turn, key or pull input
cad.opening: All furniture remains within pocket clearance when retracted
cad.load: Operating and holding loads pass into leaf reinforcement and supported closing jamb

notes: The selected leaf needs adequate solid edge material for the lock preparation and fixings.

objects.name: cavity sliding-door hook bolt
objects.definition: A hooked or beaked locking bolt projecting from a cavity-slider lock body and engaging a matching strike to resist the leaf sliding open.
functions: Engage the closing-jamb strike
Hold the sliding leaf in its closed position
Retract into the lock body for opening and pocket travel

cad.pattern: One moving bolt at the leaf closing edge
cad.placement: Within the cavity lock body facing the closing jamb
cad.opening: Retracts fully for pocket travel
cad.load: Carries sliding holding force into lock case and strike

notes: Bolt geometry must match the selected strike; a generic rectangular swing-door strike is not assumed compatible.

objects.name: cavity sliding-door lock strike
objects.definition: A strike plate fixed to the cavity-slider closing jamb and shaped to receive the selected sliding-door latch or hook bolt.
functions: Receive and retain the cavity-lock bolt
Protect the closing jamb
Transfer holding and closing loads into the frame

cad.pattern: One strike aligned with the cavity lock bolt
cad.placement: On or in the closing jamb
cad.opening: Accepts selected bolt travel and engagement
cad.load: Transfers holding and impact load into closing jamb support

notes: A box or pip strike may be selected; the actual receiving geometry is product-specific.

objects.name: cavity sliding-door strike box
objects.definition: A recessed receiving box behind a cavity-slider strike plate, providing depth and enclosure for the projected hook, bolt or latch.
functions: Provide a clear bolt pocket
Close the jamb recess
Keep debris away from the locking engagement
not_synonyms: dust box for every latch automatically

cad.pattern: One box behind a boxed cavity strike
cad.placement: Within the closing jamb behind the strike plate
cad.opening: Receives the full projected bolt or hook
cad.load: Encloses the pocket; primary holding load passes through strike and jamb

notes: Model only when included in the selected strike arrangement.

objects.name: cavity sliding-door soft-close damper
objects.definition: A track-mounted capture and damping device that engages a moving cavity-slider leaf near the end of travel and draws or slows it into the selected open or closed position.
functions: Reduce end-of-travel impact
Pull the leaf gently into its final position
Help hold the leaf at the captured position

cad.pattern: One capture device at each selected softened travel end
cad.placement: Within or adjacent to the head track
cad.opening: Operates within track and pelmet clearance
cad.load: Transfers deceleration force into track support

notes: Soft close controls motion but does not replace a latch, lock or verified travel stop unless the selected system explicitly combines those functions.

objects.name: internal folding-door hardware assembly
objects.definition: The head track, pivots, guides, inter-panel hinges, jamb bracket, aligners, stops, pulls and fixings that coordinate two or more internal door panels folding together.
functions: Support and guide folding panels
Create linked panel rotation and translation
Hold panels aligned in open and closed positions

cad.pattern: One head track and pivot-guide set per folding panel group with hinges between panels
cad.placement: Within the head and jambs of an internal opening
cad.start: Pivot jamb and closed panel line
cad.opening: Panel sweep and folded-stack projection remain explicit
cad.load: Panel weight transfers through top guide and bottom or top pivot arrangement as selected

notes: Folding hardware geometry differs from a simple sliding track and hanger system.

objects.name: internal folding-door head track
objects.definition: A horizontal channel fixed under the opening head that carries or guides the top pivot and guide hardware of an internal folding door.
functions: Guide the folding panel group
Locate top pivots and stops
Transfer selected guide or suspension loads into the frame head

cad.pattern: One continuous track across each folding-door opening or panel group
cad.placement: Under the level opening head
cad.opening: Guide and pivot components travel or seat within the channel
cad.load: Transfers guide and any suspended panel loads through fixings to the head support

notes: Track length, support and load role follow the selected kit.

objects.name: internal folding-door top pivot
objects.definition: A pivot pin and socket at the top of the jamb-side folding panel, locating the upper end of the fixed folding axis in the head track or bracket.
functions: Locate the upper pivot axis
Guide the pivot-side panel
Allow adjustment where provided

cad.pattern: One top pivot at each pivot-side panel group
cad.placement: Between panel top and track pivot socket
cad.opening: Rotates in place while panels fold
cad.load: Provides upper lateral location and carries selected vertical share if designed

notes: Top pivot and top guide may look similar but have different fixed and travelling roles.

objects.name: internal folding-door top guide
objects.definition: A travelling pin, roller or slider at the top of the guide-side folding panel that moves along the head track as the panels fold and unfold.
functions: Guide the moving panel top
Keep the folding group aligned to the track
Translate while inter-panel hinges rotate

cad.pattern: One travelling guide at the top of each guide panel
cad.placement: Between panel top and head-track channel
cad.opening: Travels along the track while rotating with the panel
cad.load: Carries lateral guide force and selected vertical support as designed

notes: Do not substitute the generic cavity-slider hanger: a folding guide follows coupled rotation and translation.

objects.name: internal folding-door bottom pivot
objects.definition: The lower pivot pin and adjustment fitting at the jamb-side folding panel, seating in a floor or jamb bracket and forming the lower end of the pivot axis.
functions: Support and locate the pivot-side panel
Define the lower folding axis
Provide vertical or horizontal adjustment where selected

cad.pattern: One bottom pivot per pivot-side folding panel group
cad.placement: Between panel bottom and jamb or floor bracket
cad.opening: Rotates while remaining at the fixed pivot location
cad.load: Often carries panel vertical load into bracket and floor or jamb support

notes: Its bracket and substrate must carry the selected load and remain coordinated with floor finishes.

objects.name: internal folding-door bottom jamb bracket
objects.definition: A bracket fixed at the floor and pivot jamb that contains or supports the bottom pivot socket of a folding-door panel group.
functions: Anchor the lower pivot position
Transfer pivot loads into the floor and jamb
Allow selected horizontal adjustment

cad.pattern: One bracket at each folding-group pivot jamb
cad.placement: At the intersection of finished floor and pivot jamb
cad.opening: Sits outside the required panel swing and circulation as designed
cad.load: Transfers pivot vertical and lateral reactions into floor and jamb

notes: Fixings must suit both substrates and should not compromise waterproofing where present.

objects.name: internal folding-door inter-panel hinge
objects.definition: A hinge connecting two neighbouring folding-door panels so they rotate relative to each other while moving as a linked pair or group.
functions: Join folding panels
Create the alternating fold axis
Transfer panel loads and operating force between leaves

cad.pattern: Two or more hinges aligned along each connected panel pair
cad.placement: Between meeting vertical edges of folding panels
cad.opening: Fold axis and knuckle clearance permit the selected stack direction
cad.load: Transfers relative panel forces across the connected edges

notes: The hinge side alternates with folding direction and cannot be inferred from panel count alone.

objects.name: internal folding-door panel aligner
objects.definition: A small paired fitting on multi-panel folding doors that brings adjacent guide panels into alignment when the assembly reaches the closed position.
functions: Align meeting panels when closed
Reduce stepped or twisted panel faces
Support stable four-panel meeting geometry

cad.pattern: Paired aligners at the nominated height on meeting guide panels
cad.placement: On concealed panel faces near the lower meeting zone
cad.opening: Disengages as panels fold
cad.load: Carries light alignment force, not panel support load

notes: Used where the selected multi-panel kit requires it; not every two-panel bifold has a separate aligner.

objects.name: internal folding-door track stop
objects.definition: An adjustable stop within a folding-door head track that contacts the top guide or related hardware to set the final panel position and resist over-travel.
functions: Set the closed or open guide position
Limit guide travel
Apply light positioning pressure where the selected kit provides it

cad.pattern: One or more stops at selected guide travel limits
cad.placement: Inside the folding-door head track
cad.opening: Sets final guide position without obstructing folding movement
cad.load: Transfers light end force into the track

notes: Folding-track stop belongs to coupled panel hardware and is not merged with the generic sliding-door stop.
